correctness.rationale: For every \(1\le k\le n\), the lower bound follows because never-moved elements define a block matching, while the upper bound pads both partitions to \(k\) labeled slots, extends a maximum-weight matching to a slot bijection, and recolors each mismatched element once. Forgetting labels produces a Bell-graph walk with at most \(k\) blocks; the lower bound forces equality. The diameter bound follows because a random slot permutation has expected overlap \(n/k\), and a balanced \(k\)-block partition versus the indiscrete partition attains equality. Exhaustive all-pairs checks through \(n=6\) agree.

value.rationale: The result gives the complete all-pairs shortest-path metric and exact diameter for a canonical two-parameter family at the foundation of Bell-colouring reconfiguration. It also proves the non-obvious isometry of every block-capped induced subgraph and reduces shortest reconfiguration to one assignment problem. This is structural information not supplied by the recent Hamiltonicity or reconstruction theorems and is more than a finite computation or routine parameter substitution.
